summary: This article explains what germs are, how they spread from hands to bodies, how soap and water remove them, and how and when to wash your hands.
introduce: Write First, Next, Then, and Finally on the board and ask a volunteer to use them to describe how they get ready for school. Tell students to watch for the order of events as they read “Germs and Handwashing”.

keyTerms.def: a tool that makes very tiny things look much bigger
very tiny living things; some are helpful and some cause illness
a very tiny germ that can make people or animals sick

challengeTerms.def: a living thing too small to see without a microscope
the passing of something from one person or place to another
an illness caused by germs getting into the body

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that washing your hands is the most important thing you can do to stay healthy? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Make a poster message for your school bathroom.
struggling: Pre-teach microscope, bacteria, and virus with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers put sentence strips of the main events in order before writing.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use microorganism, transmission, and infection in a short paragraph that summarizes the key events in order and explain which step matters most.
